issues.detail: Hebrew 'מִיָּמָי' means 'from my days' i.e. 'in all my days' / 'all my life', but Chinese '從我日中' reads as 'from my days' literally, which is awkward; more importantly, the Hebrew 'לֹא יֶחֱרַף לְבָבִי' means 'my heart will not reproach/taunt me' (i.e. my heart will not condemn me), but Chinese '我的心必不從我日中蒙羞' renders it as 'my heart will not be put to shame from my days', changing the subject/action: Hebrew has the heart as the agent of reproach, Chinese makes the heart the object of shame. This alters who is doing what.
